findings.problem: In everyday Latin American speech, 'to laugh' is almost always the pronominal reírse, so 'ríe mucho' without se sounds literary rather than conversational.
findings.fix: example.es: Mi hija se ríe mucho con ese programa.

findings.problem: The sentence leaves out the 'se' that natural speech uses with this verb, so the learner memorizes a stiff pattern.
findings.fix: example.es: Mi hija se ríe mucho con ese programa.

back.example: My daughter laughs a lot with that show.

note: Consider having the grammar or example show that the everyday form is reírse (me río, te ríes, se ríe), since learners will mostly hear it that way.
